title: Session-aware trace summarizer and hybrid SLO estimator for multi-tenant latency bursts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: High-cardinality tracing for multi-tenant workloads is expensive and noisy; current burn-rate alerts produce many false positives for short-lived session spikes. Goal: Build an experiment that (1) summarizes per-session traces with lightweight lossy compression in a sidecar/collector, (2) combines summarized trace latency signals with metric-based SLO estimators (hybrid estimator) to improve burst detection precision, and (3) apply an anomaly score to reduce pager noise and avoid paging for expected bursty sessions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end pipeline demonstrates >=50% reduction in trace storage for sampled sessions without losing top-95 latency spike signals. 2) Hybrid SLO estimator reduces false positive burn-rate alerts by >=30% on historical replay datasets. 3) Pager rate for targeted services decreases by >=20% during A/B experiment compared to control. 4) Dashboards show trace-summary -> slo estimator lineage and explainability for flagged incidents.
implementation_notes: Architecture: deploy a session-aware summarizer as a lightweight collector sidecar or ingest-stage transform. Summarizer outputs compact span summaries (session_id, percentile sketches, top-span hashes, culprit-tags) to the backend. Hybrid estimator blends fast metric-derived SLO (windowed latency histograms) with infrequent summarized-trace corrections to adjust burn-rate weights. Anomaly scorer uses session context (customer tier, request path, burstiness history) and outputs suppression hints for the paging policy.
workplan: Week 1: Prototype summarizer logic (trace->session mapping, single-pass percentile sketch).
Week 2: Ingest adapter to accept summaries and store compactly; replay historical traces for fidelity testing.
Week 3: Implement hybrid SLO estimator and offline replay evaluation against 6 weeks of production telemetry.
Week 4: Build anomaly scorer and integrate with paging policy simulator; run canary A/B on non-customer-critical namespace.
Week 5: Dashboarding and runbook: add trace-summary visualizations, confidence bands, and rollout playbook.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Session stitching may be incomplete for some ingress patterns -> Mitigation: fall back to request-path level summarization and add TTL heuristics.
Risk: Summaries might omit a subtle tail-causing span -> Mitigation: sample full traces when summary detects unusual internal variance (adaptive full-trace capture).

Risk: New estimator could suppress real incidents for enterprise customers -> Mitigation: tiered policies that disable suppression for high-SLA customers and require explicit opt-in for suppression in Dedicated/Private deployments.
experimental_notes: We will run an A/B test on two cohorts: 5% of traffic for canary (summaries + hybrid estimator) and 5% control (status-quo). Use deterministic hashing by org-id to split. Replays will use labels/tags to evaluate historical false positives. Success gate is both statistical improvement on replay and no missed SEV rollups in canary window.
